title: Payroll
tagline: Get every transaction and time card in before payroll signs off.
learningObjectives: Know your two deadlines from the payroll calendar: the HCM transaction cutoff and when time cards are due.
Get time card problems to the right manager, and help them fix them.
Make sure non-exempt overtime is paid, even when it wasn't approved in advance.
Chase late approvals, then escalate. Never approve for the manager.
Enter retro changes with the approved effective date, before the HCM transaction cutoff.
Catch errors in your final time card check, before payroll signs off.
briefing: Morning. It's Thursday, Oct 22. We're in pay period 22, Oct 11 to Oct 24. These dates come straight from the real 2026 payroll calendar.

Two deadlines run your week. Transactions close at the HCM transaction cutoff this Friday, Oct 23. Time cards are due Monday, Oct 26 at noon. Then payroll signs off and runs payroll. We don't run payroll; we make sure what they get is right.
Your job: get transactions in before Friday's cutoff, check time cards, get problems to the right manager and help them fix them, and make sure every time card is approved by Monday at noon.
Requests land in your inbox through the day. Some are urgent; some are noise. On pay day, Friday Oct 30, you'll see what your decisions did.

payday.clean: Clean pay day. Nobody at your desk with a pay stub. That is what good payroll support looks like: nothing happens.
payday.problems: Some problems reached people's paychecks. Let's trace each one back to the decision that caused it.

noise.subject: Lunch and learn moved to next Wednesday
noise.body: The November lunch and learn moved to next Wednesday at noon. No action needed.

noise.subject: Garage resurfacing next Monday
noise.body: The staff garage closes next Monday morning for resurfacing. Plan for the overflow lot.

noise.subject: Printer is jammed again
noise.body: The second floor printer is jammed. I put a sign on it.

steps.title: Read the payroll calendar

opener.speaker: coach
opener.line: These dates come straight from the real payroll calendar. Before you open anything, tell me how this week works.

steps.context: Renee taps the 2026 payroll calendar pinned to the bulletin board.

attachment.title: 2026 Payroll Calendar, biweekly period 22
lines: Pay period: Sun Oct 11 to Sat Oct 24
Time cards due: Mon Oct 26 at noon

steps.hint: Transactions and time cards don't share a deadline. One of them closes before the pay period even ends.

choices.text: Transactions, like a raise, must be entered and approved by Friday's HCM transaction cutoff. Time cards must be approved by Monday at noon.
choices.feedback: Right. Two deadlines, two kinds of work. Transactions close Friday, before the period even ends on Saturday. Time cards close Monday at noon, then payroll signs off and runs payroll. Next time: put both dates on your calendar at the start of every period.

choices.text: Everything is due Monday at noon, when time cards are due.
choices.feedback: Time cards are due Monday at noon, but transactions close earlier, at Friday's HCM transaction cutoff. A raise entered Monday misses this payroll. Next time: check both dates on the payroll calendar.

choices.text: Nothing is due until the paycheck date, Fri Oct 30.
choices.feedback: The paycheck date is when people see the result. By then payroll has already run. Next time: work back from the HCM transaction cutoff and the time card deadline.

steps.title: Send the time card reminder

opener.speaker: coach
opener.line: Week two time cards are still in progress. Let's get a reminder out, so everything's approved by Monday at noon.

steps.context: Week 2 time cards are still in progress. Send a reminder so employees finish their time and managers approve it by Monday at noon.
steps.hint: Who has to act before Monday at noon? It isn't only the employees.

decisions.label: Send
decisions.prompt: When should the reminder go out?

choices.text: Today, Thursday, so people can fix gaps before the weekend
choices.feedback: Thursday gives employees two workdays to finish their time and gives managers a clear target: approved by Monday at noon. Next time: send it two workdays before the time card deadline, every period.

totalsAdjust.note: Wed Oct 21 entered after your reminder

choices.text: Monday morning, right before the deadline
choices.feedback: Monday morning leaves managers a few hours to approve, and anyone out Monday can't fix their time. Next time: send it before the weekend.

consequences.speaker: emp_grant
consequences.line: My check is short. I saw the reminder Monday, but I was out and couldn't add Wednesday's hours in time.
consequences.summary: Aisha's Wednesday hours missed the run.

choices.text: Monday at 11:30 AM, as a last call
choices.feedback: Thirty minutes before the deadline is too late to change anything. Next time: send it before the weekend.

consequences.speaker: emp_grant
consequences.line: The reminder came half an hour before the deadline. My Wednesday hours aren't on my check.
consequences.summary: Aisha's Wednesday hours missed the run.

choices.text: Non-exempt employees and their managers
choices.feedback: Employees finish their time; managers see the approval deadline. Both have to act. Next time: always include the approvers.

choices.text: Only employees with incomplete time cards
choices.feedback: Employees can finish their time, but nobody told managers the deadline. Late approvals are the most common reason time misses a run. Next time: include managers.

choices.text: Everyone in the department, including exempt staff
choices.feedback: Exempt staff don't submit time cards here, so the message is noise for them, and people learn to ignore your reminders. Next time: send it to the people who have to act. [SME] Confirm which exempt groups, if any, record time.

steps.title: Weekly time card check

opener.speaker: coach
opener.line: Your weekly check turned up three exceptions. Remember, managers review their own team's time. Spot the problem, get it to the right manager, and help them fix it.

steps.context: Your weekly time card check shows three exceptions in period 22. Managers review their team's time and ask employees about anything unclear. Your job is to spot problems, get them to the right manager, and help them fix them.
steps.hint: For each exception, ask: whose employee is this, and what does that manager need from you to fix it?

grid.caption: Timecard Review · period 22, Oct 11 to Oct 24 (week 1: Oct 11 to 17)

decisions.label: Jordan Reyes, Tue Oct 20
decisions.prompt: Jordan clocked in at 8:00 and has no out punch. Jordan usually leaves at 5:00 and reports to Marcus Bell. What do you do?

choices.text: Send Marcus the details (Jordan, Tue Oct 20, no out punch). Ask him to confirm the out time with Jordan and correct it before Monday at noon, and offer to walk him through the fix.
choices.feedback: Marcus checked with Jordan, who left at 3:30 for an appointment, and fixed the punch with your help. The manager reviewed it, the record is right, and nobody guessed. Next time: same move. Route it to the manager and support the fix.

totalsAdjust.note: Tue out 3:30 PM, corrected by Marcus

choices.text: Enter a 5:00 PM out punch yourself. That's Jordan's normal schedule.
choices.feedback: Jordan left at 3:30 that day, so you just paid 1.5 hours that weren't worked, and Marcus never reviewed it. Next time: send it to the manager to confirm with the employee.

totalsAdjust.note: Tue out 5:00 PM, entered by HCM

consequences.speaker: emp_reyes
consequences.line: Quick thing. I left at 3:30 on the 20th for a doctor visit, but I was paid for a full day. I don't want that coming back on me.
consequences.summary: Overpayment to Jordan. Recovery task next period.
consequences.task: Work with payroll to recover 1.5 hours overpaid to Jordan Reyes.

choices.text: Ask Jordan for the out time and correct the punch yourself.
choices.feedback: Jordan said 3:30, so the hours are right, but Marcus never saw it. Managers review their team's time and ask their employees about it; you support them. Next time: route it to the manager and help them fix it.

totalsAdjust.note: Tue out 3:30 PM, entered by HCM

choices.text: Leave it. Jordan will notice and fix it.
choices.feedback: A missing punch means Tuesday doesn't pay at all, and Marcus approves a card with a hole in it. Next time: get every exception to the manager before the deadline.

consequences.speaker: emp_reyes
consequences.line: My check is missing all of Tuesday the 20th. I have rent due.
consequences.summary: Jordan was underpaid a full day.
consequences.task: Work with payroll on an off-cycle payment for Jordan's missing Tuesday.

spoken.speaker: mgr_ortiz
spoken.line: Priya put down 44 hours in week 1, and I never approved overtime. Can I just change her time to 40?

decisions.label: Priya Nair, week 1
decisions.prompt: Priya worked 44 hours in week 1 setting up the fall event. Dana Ortiz didn't approve overtime in advance and left a note: "I didn't approve OT. Can I change her time to 40?" What do you tell Dana?

choices.text: The 4 hours must be paid as overtime, approved or not. Pre-approval is a conversation she can have with Priya.
choices.feedback: Correct. Federal law requires paying non-exempt staff overtime for hours over 40 in a workweek, approved or not. Dana handles the approval issue with Priya; the time stays as worked. Next time: same answer, and point the manager to the policy.

choices.text: She can move 4 hours into week 2 so Priya stays at 40.
choices.feedback: Overtime is counted per workweek. Moving hours into another week to avoid it is a wage and hour violation, and it falsifies the record. Next time: the time stays as worked, and the overtime is paid.

totalsAdjust.note: 4 hours moved to week 2 by manager

consequences.speaker: emp_nair
consequences.line: My overtime from the event setup isn't here, and week 2 shows hours I didn't work. Who changed my time card?
consequences.summary: Priya's overtime was moved. Wage and hour exposure.
consequences.task: Correct Priya's time card and pay the overtime.

choices.text: Yes. Since overtime wasn't approved, she can change it to 40.
choices.feedback: Hours worked must be paid, and hours over 40 in a workweek at 1.5 times the regular rate, approved or not. Cutting the time underpays Priya and falsifies the record. Next time: tell the manager the time stays as worked.

consequences.speaker: emp_nair
consequences.line: I worked 44 hours that week. Why was I paid for 40?
consequences.summary: Priya was underpaid 4 hours of overtime.
consequences.task: Work with payroll to pay Priya's missing overtime.

decisions.label: Sam Okafor, Wed Oct 21
decisions.prompt: Sam entered 5 hours worked and 3 hours of PTO. Sam reports to Dana Ortiz. What do you do?

choices.text: Let Dana know non-exempt PTO goes in 4-hour increments. She confirms Sam's actual hours with Sam, and the entry is corrected before she approves.
choices.feedback: Sam worked 4 hours and takes 4 hours of PTO. The entry follows policy, and Dana confirmed it with Sam. Next time: same move, and mention the increment in your reminder.

totalsAdjust.note: Wed 4.0 worked + PTO 4.0, confirmed by Dana

choices.text: Leave it. 5 plus 3 adds up to 8.
choices.feedback: Non-exempt PTO is entered in 4-hour increments. A 3-hour entry can be rejected or throw off Sam's balance. Next time: catch it in your weekly check and get it to the manager.

choices.text: Change it to 4 hours of PTO and 4 worked yourself.
choices.feedback: The math may be right, but you changed someone's worked time without Sam or Dana confirming it. Next time: get it to the manager to confirm with the employee.

steps.title: Enter a retro pay increase

opener.speaker: mgr_bell
opener.line: Jordan's raise finally came through. The approval letter's attached. Can you get it in before Friday's cutoff?

steps.context: Marcus Bell sent Jordan Reyes's approved raise, with the approval letter attached.

attachment.title: Pay increase approval
lines: Effective date: Sunday, September 27 (start of pay period 21)

steps.hint: The approval letter answers both fields. Copy, don't calculate. Then make sure it's in before Friday's cutoff.

choices.text: Sun Sep 27
choices.feedback: Sep 27 is the date on the approved letter. Entered before Friday's HCM transaction cutoff, the raise makes this payroll, and payroll pays Jordan the difference for period 21. Next time: always use the document's effective date, even when it's in the past.

consequences.speaker: emp_reyes
consequences.line: My raise and the back pay for September came through. Thank you for getting it in before the cutoff.
consequences.summary: Jordan received the raise and retro pay.

choices.text: Sun Oct 11, start of this period
choices.feedback: Starting the raise this period drops the two weeks of back pay Jordan is owed for period 21. Next time: use the effective date on the approved document.

consequences.speaker: emp_reyes
consequences.line: I was told my raise went back to September 27. The back pay isn't here.
consequences.summary: Jordan was shorted two weeks of retro pay.
consequences.task: Correct the effective date and get the missing retro pay processed.

choices.text: Thu Oct 22, today
choices.feedback: Today's date ignores the approved effective date, so almost four weeks of back pay is missing. Next time: use the effective date on the approved document.

consequences.speaker: emp_reyes
consequences.line: My raise only shows for the last few days. It was supposed to start September 27.
consequences.summary: Jordan was shorted almost four weeks of retro pay.
consequences.task: Correct the effective date and get the missing retro pay processed.

choices.text: Not entered
choices.feedback: The raise wasn't entered and approved by Friday's HCM transaction cutoff, so it waits for the next payroll, with retro. Next time: enter transactions the day they arrive and leave time for every approver.

consequences.speaker: mgr_bell
consequences.line: I sent Jordan's raise Thursday morning. Why isn't it on this check?
consequences.summary: Jordan's raise missed the HCM transaction cutoff.

choices.feedback: $24.50 matches the approval letter. Next time: same. Read it off the document.

choices.text: Other amount
choices.feedback: The rate doesn't match the approval letter, so every hour since Sep 27 pays wrong. Next time: copy the rate straight from the approved document and check it twice.

consequences.speaker: emp_reyes
consequences.line: My new rate on the pay stub doesn't match my letter.
consequences.summary: Jordan's new rate was keyed wrong.
consequences.task: Correct Jordan's rate and settle the difference.

choices.text: Not entered
choices.feedback: The rate wasn't entered before the HCM transaction cutoff.

steps.title: Chase late approvals

opener.speaker: coach
opener.line: It's Monday, and time cards are due at noon. Marcus still has three waiting on him.

steps.context: Monday, 8:00 AM. Time cards are due at noon. In Timecard Review, Approval State shows Submitted for Jordan Reyes, Tomás Rivera, and Aisha Grant on Marcus Bell's team. Dana Ortiz's team shows Approved (PayPrep Ready).
steps.hint: You can make it easy for Marcus. You can't do it for him.

choices.text: Email Marcus the three names, the pay period, and the noon deadline, and ask who his backup approver is if he's out.
choices.feedback: Specific names, the period, the deadline, and a backup plan. That's a reminder a manager can act on in a minute. Next time: same, and ask about the backup before you need one.

choices.text: Approve the three time cards yourself. You've already checked them.
choices.feedback: You can see the time cards, but approving them is the manager attesting that the time is right. Doing it for Marcus removes his review, even if the hours look fine. Next time: remind, then escalate. Never approve for the manager.

consequences.speaker: mgr_bell
consequences.line: Audit flagged approvals on my team that I never made. I need to know why.
consequences.summary: Approvals made for a manager were flagged.

choices.text: Wait. Marcus usually approves Monday morning.
choices.feedback: Usually isn't a plan. If Marcus is out today, you find out with no time to spare. Next time: remind first thing, with names and the deadline.

steps.title: Final time card check

opener.speaker: coach
opener.line: Before payroll signs off at noon, check the totals one more time. Lena updated her time card Thursday night.

steps.context: Before payroll signs off at noon, check the period 22 totals for Dana's and Marcus's teams. Lena Kowalski updated her time card Thursday night. Flag anything that needs a closer look.
steps.hint: A normal two weeks is about 80 hours. Look for anything far from that.

review.caption: Timecard totals · period 22, Oct 11 to Oct 24

decisions.prompt: Flag the rows that need a closer look, then submit.

choices.text: Flagged Lena Kowalski
choices.feedback: Lena's Thursday shows 80.0 hours. She meant 8.0, and Dana approved it without noticing. Catching it before payroll signs off saves a $2,376 overpayment and a recovery conversation. Next time: scan totals for anything far from a normal 80.

choices.text: Did not flag Lena Kowalski
choices.feedback: Lena's Thursday shows 80.0 hours instead of 8.0. Dana approved it, payroll signed off, and Lena was overpaid $2,376. Next time: scan totals for anything far from a normal 80 before the deadline.

consequences.speaker: emp_kowalski
consequences.line: My check is huge. I think I typed 80 instead of 8 on Thursday. I don't want to spend money that isn't mine.
consequences.summary: Lena was overpaid $2,376. Recovery task next period.
consequences.task: Work with payroll to recover $2,376 overpaid to Lena Kowalski.

decisions.prompt: Lena confirms she meant 8.0, and Dana already approved her time card. How does it get fixed before noon?

choices.text: Tell Dana. She removes her approval, Lena corrects Thursday to 8.0, and Dana approves again before noon.
choices.feedback: The employee fixes her own entry, and the manager reviews it again before payroll signs off. Clean record. Next time: same order.

totalsAdjust.note: Corrected to 8.0 by Lena, approved again by Dana

choices.text: Change 80.0 to 8.0 yourself. It's obviously a typo.
choices.feedback: The number is right, but now the record shows you changed an approved time card with nothing from Lena or Dana. Next time: the employee corrects it and the manager approves it again.

choices.text: Leave it approved and ask payroll to fix it after they sign off.
choices.feedback: Once payroll signs off, the approval can't be removed until payroll removes the sign-off, and the 80 hours can pay. You had time to fix it before noon. Next time: fix what you can before the deadline, and bring payroll only what you can't resolve.

consequences.speaker: emp_kowalski
consequences.line: My check was way too big, and now there's a recovery. I told everyone Thursday was a typo.
consequences.summary: Lena was overpaid $2,376 after a fixable error.
consequences.task: Work with payroll to recover $2,376 overpaid to Lena Kowalski.

steps.title: Marcus is out today

opener.speaker: coach
opener.line: Marcus just set his out of office. He's out sick today, and his team's time cards are still waiting.

steps.context: Marcus Bell's out of office: "Out sick today, back Tuesday." Jordan, Tomás, and Aisha still show Submitted. Time cards are due at noon.
steps.hint: Whose job is it when the approver can't approve?

decisions.prompt: It's Monday morning. What do you do?

choices.text: Send the three names, the pay period, and the noon deadline to Marcus's backup approver, and copy Dr. Park as his supervisor.
choices.feedback: The backup approver approves by 11:00. The review stays with a manager, and nobody misses pay. Next time: same. Escalate early, with the names and deadline. [SME] Confirm Vanderbilt's backup approver rule.

choices.text: Approve them yourself. Marcus is out, and people need to be paid.
choices.feedback: Good intent, wrong control. Approving as the manager removes the manager's review. Next time: escalate to the backup approver or supervisor.

consequences.speaker: mgr_bell
consequences.line: I came back to find my team's time approved without me. That can't happen.
consequences.summary: Approvals made for a manager were flagged.

choices.text: Leave them. Unapproved time gets picked up in the next run.
choices.feedback: Three people's week 2 hours miss this run. Next time: escalate to the backup approver before the deadline. [SME] Confirm what happens to unapproved time at Vanderbilt.

consequences.speaker: emp_rivera
consequences.line: Half my hours aren't on this check. Jordan and Aisha are saying the same thing.
consequences.summary: Three employees' hours missed the run.
consequences.task: Work with payroll on off-cycle payments for three employees.
